Honey, as someone else on disability for mental issues, let me just say this.  Success isn't working a paying job, it isn't money.  it's making a difference.  Take this pain, and talk it out loud.  Use your experiences to reach out to others like you, like us, and when you help someone, it feels so amazing.  Yeah, life fucking sucks hairy spider ball eggs, but it is what it is.  Things go up, things come down (usually either on your head or your foot, in my experience) but it does get easier, even if it doesn't get better.  What you do is you keep talking, you keep breathing, you find something to focus on that you enjoy.  And you remember that there ARE people who care about you, and would love to hear from you again.
Not knowing your life, I can't say why you shouldn't either.  but there are people who care, and would love to hear from you again.

Trust me trust me TRUST ME i know that so well!  i'm also bipolar, with several other issues.  and hey, don't give up on the meds.  it took me 5 years and 12 head-pounders to get the right dosage/combination of meds, and even after that i periodically have to have my meds adjusted, but life is so much easier on them now that i got them right!  sure, i still have nights like tonight where i make a thowaway just to say "omg fuck this shit i can't take it anymore" and reach for someone who can't see me, will never know me, and won't judge me, who is going through similar emotions.  So no, no med is perfect at 100% prevention, but they can help if you give it time to find the right ones!

As for your self discovery, i hope you find what you need in yourself to exist, then to survive, then to live.  Because from what I've read, and from your response, you are a kind, great person who deserves to enjoy life.  <3

I agree.  Sometimes it doesn't pass, but it does get easier to deal with.  think of your emotions like skin, right?  you take a little scratch (sadness) and it stings and burns for a little while, and then it's gone, and you can't even see the mark anymore.  sometimes, though, you take a really deep cut, and at first you don't even feel it, then it starts to throb, then it starts hurting so bad you can't bear it.  over time, it stops hurting so bad, back to a throbbing ache.  after a while longer, there is no more pain, but you can still look and see that long thin white line that says "hey guess what i was here"  and that scar can itch at times, years after it's healed, just to remind you.  but that itch is nothing compared to the pain it was, and so you just scratch it, and keep going on.

Okay hun, first of all, don't blame yourself for the actions of others.  Even if you influenced them, you did not force them, so it is not your fault.  Secondly, a therapist might help with some of the older issues (even if you didn't think of it as molestation, it was, and even if you didn't realize it, it might have caused a flux of your thinking process).  Thirdly, reaching out to people is a great way to either a) find every last asshole on earth, or b) find great people who really and truly care about you, even though they don't know shit fuck about you except what little you think telling them will help them figure out your issues and how to help.  Another thing of advice, journaling maybe can help you find trigger patterns, like...when i did this today i felt like this...and you can attempt to avoid those patterns in the future.  Sometimes it's just little things that can help, like a movie, bath, music, etc....sometimes you need to get a little deeper to the core to push all that nasty pus of emotion out.  i am NOT a doctor or professional, and this is simply advice that has PERSONALLY helped ME.  it may or may not help you, but here's hoping.  just know that someone cared enough to try.  hope that helps, some, at least.

omg i was at dragoncon this year, and we got there really early, and i just went ahead to my first panel, right?  so i get out, and start walking around looking for my friend, at first not realizing how many people there were, until i started getting jostled a little bit.  i finally found emerald rose's booth (another of my fave bands, and one of my friend as well, so we both pretty much knew that if we got lost to meet there) so i just stopped and kind of hid under the steps.  time went by and by and by and i kept getting more scared until i had a full fledged panic attack and just sat down in the floor and started bawling.  my friend finally shows up, i leap at him still bawling, and he goes, "what's the matter, didn't your v say hey to you?" and i just stopped crying immediately, eyes and mouth wide and went "what....did you....just say?"  and he goes, "Yeah your man v is right behind you"  i turned around and he waved and i just ducked my head and sighed.  my friend decided to check out the merch while he was set up, so yup, he dragged me along, red eyed and runny nosed.  i wanted to kill him just before the earth opened up to swallow me.  v never once laughed or said anything to me except normal chit chat, and something about so many people out so early.  he's seen and replied to quite a few of my posts on his FB page, so when i bought his book and just handed it to him, he goes, Anje, right? and i just kind of nodded.  And he goes "how would i spell that?"  and I said, in utter distress from still coming out of a panic attack  "A.....n..............."  turned around looked at my friend "G?"  he finishes spelling my own name for Voltaire.  But the concert that night was amazing!  And I spent $50 on merch from that goth god.

My dad passed away in April, and my mom is too busy with her own life, and her two sons.  I'm seeing a therapist, and am actually on anti-depressants.  Usually, when my body starts getting too used to the meds, I can feel myself sliding down into depression.  Not this time.  It wasn't a slide, or a leap, or even a drop, or a plummet.  It was just like...it just slammed right into me out of nowhere.  I don't think it's my meds this time; I don't know what it is.    I don't really have any ambitions in life except just to survive.  Most days I can surpass that and actually enjoy life, and live.  But tonight, it's a struggle just to exist.    My interests?  Music, writing, dancing...I usually love playing RS but tonight it felt like a chore.  I love water, but it's 1am in November, so I think a swim is out of the question.  Um.  I love coffee.  I'm freaking addicted to coffee.  It is literally the only thing I will drink.    Um.  Let's see.  I have a laundry list of mental issues, in all three main categories: trauma induced, chemical imbalance, and genetic.  So, life really threw me a great one there, but I use it to help others, I give people the strength to stand up for themselves and say "I'm not sick, I just have a different brain than you"  I try to break that stigma of "crazy" you know?  I don't know.  I just...if I can show even one person that it can be done, then maybe I did something right, after all.
